A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScaleQuest and contain readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training evaluations, component ablations, scaling experiments, and synthetic-data analyses, including Table 1 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds human evaluation, contamination analysis, code reasoning, long-chain-of-thought experiments, and further controlled comparisons.

M1.justification: The core QFT, QPO, question-filtering, and reward-selection pipeline remains unchanged. Appendix D adds ScaleQuest-Simple, using Qwen2-Math-7B-Instruct across stages previously assigned to several models; Appendix C.2 also reports adapting the QPO prompts for code reasoning.

E1.justification: v2 extends the mathematics-only experiments to CodeFeedback-derived training data and HumanEval, MBPP, and BigCodeBench evaluation. It also adds GSM-Hard numerical shifts, MathChat follow-up questions and error correction, and long-CoT evaluation including AIME24 and AMC25, as labeled in Table 8.

E2.justification: New comparisons include CodeFeedback-Filtered and its response-enhanced CFB-Aug variant in Table 9, and Llama3.1-70B-Instruct as a question optimizer in Figure 4. Conversely, v1 Figure 1's model-ranking comparison, including Claude-3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro, disappears. Table 1's mathematics comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include human ratings of 40 examples per dataset on 1–5 scales, approximately 400K-example controlled comparisons, and QPO training-volume experiments spanning 5K–40K examples. For the retained component ablation, v1 specifies GPT-4o-mini as judge, whereas v2 refers to the GPT-4o evaluation in Section 2.3; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a 13-gram contamination analysis, human assessment of question quality, QPO data-volume sensitivity, and evaluation of a simplified pipeline. It also tests numerical and conversational robustness and extends the controlled question-quality comparison to three additional backbones. The original component and generator-mixture ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added evaluations continue to report point estimates; the human-study sample count does not establish repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but Figure 5 revises raw-model GSM8K/MATH/College Math/OlympiadBench scores from 70.9/43.0/35.2/12.3 to 75.9/47.7/38.2/14.6. Substantial new results include teacher versus fine-tuned long-CoT averages of 75.0 versus 81.8, and code averages of 64.0/69.3/69.9 for CFB/CFB-Aug/ScaleQuest. Human, contamination, robustness, and controlled-comparison results are also added.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Equation 3's explicit definition of the linear difficulty-score head, its MSE expression, and variable explanations, retaining only a prose description of the scorer and MSE training. The instruction-tuning and QPO equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central low-cost, scalable synthesis contribution remains, but v2 adds demonstrated code generalization to the abstract and long-CoT applicability to the introduction. It also removes the abstract/conclusion claims of surpassing GPT-4-Turbo, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, and all competitors in the 7B–70B range, substantially narrowing those headline comparisons.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive model-selection guidance distinguishing domain-specific generators from general-purpose preference-data optimizers. The human evaluation introduces a qualified comparison with human-curated questions, and Section 3.2 acknowledges unmatched training volumes. The limitations now emphasize uncertain effectiveness with larger models and insufficient generation quality, replacing much of v1's expansion and self-improvement agenda.

D1.justification: v2 documents model choices, sampling amounts, and the code evaluation script for the extensions; most original hyperparameters simply move to Appendix A. It omits the explicit difficulty-head specification and v1's explanation of reevaluating released comparators or retraining unavailable ones. The access pointer changes from a direct repository link to a project page, without establishing a change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting code reasoning, DeepSeek-R1, MathChat, RewardBench, and contamination checking, while removing the cited works on reformatted alignment and scaling mathematical reasoning. The central positioning against question-driven and knowledge-driven synthesis remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, method and baseline descriptions are condensed, and the related-work discussion and conclusion are substantially shortened. Hyperparameters move into a dedicated appendix, limitations become a separate section, and the appendix structure expands from two sections to six. These are substantial editorial and organizational changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Figure 1 drops its model-ranking panel and redesigns the scaling display; Figure 4 gains an optimizer comparison, and several tables are compacted. New evaluation tables and a sensitivity plot are added, while retained prompts and examples receive new typography, colors, and placement.

improvement.justification: The contamination check, additional controlled comparisons, and code-transfer experiments materially strengthen evidence for question quality and generalization, while narrower headline claims improve calibration. Reporting weaknesses remain: human-evaluation prose claims better reasonableness despite Table 5's tie, and Table 12 reports a Mistral OlympiadBench score inconsistent with Table 1. These issues and the continued absence of uncertainty estimates temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial evidential improvement.
